import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 2.28

by A. I. Kokorin

Can every orderable group be embedded in a pro-orderable group?

A group is orderable if it admits a bi-invariant linear order. A group is
pro-orderable if each bi-invariant partial order on it extends to a
bi-invariant linear order.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.28»

/-- A relation on a group is bi-invariant if multiplication on either side
preserves it. -/
def IsBiInvariant {G : Type*} [Group G] (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ a b c : G, r a b → r (c * a) (c * b)) ∧
  (∀ a b c : G, r a b → r (a * c) (b * c))

/-- A group is orderable if it admits a bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G r ∧ IsBiInvariant r

/-- A group is pro-orderable if every bi-invariant partial order on it extends
to a bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ r : G → G → Prop, IsPartialOrder G r → IsBiInvariant r →
    ∃ s : G → G → Prop,
      IsLinearOrder G s ∧ IsBiInvariant s ∧ ∀ a b : G, r a b → s a b

/--
Can every orderable group be embedded in a pro-orderable group?

The embedding is an injective group homomorphism; it is not required to
preserve any order.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.28» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsOrderable G →
      ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), IsProOrderable H ∧
        ∃ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.28»
modeling_decisions: An orderable group is modeled as a group admitting a linear-order relation invariant under multiplication on both the left and the right.
A pro-orderable group is modeled as one for which every bi-invariant partial-order relation is contained in a bi-invariant linear-order relation.
The embedding is an injective `MonoidHom` between groups; such a homomorphism preserves inverses automatically, and no order-preservation condition is imposed.
The theorem follows the repository convention of quantifying over small types using `Type`, as in neighboring Kourovka files.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 2.28

by A. I. Kokorin

Can every orderable group be embedded in a pro-orderable group?

Here an *orderable group* is a group admitting a bi-invariant (two-sided invariant) linear
order, i.e. a linear order $\le$ with $a \le b \implies xay \le xby$ for all $x, y$.
Following Problem 1.35 of the notebook, a group is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group in the sense
of Fuchs) if every bi-invariant partial order on it can be extended to a bi-invariant linear
order. "Embedded" means that there is an injective group homomorphism; no compatibility with
any order is required.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.28»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A binary relation $r$ on a group is *bi-invariant* (two-sided invariant) if
$r(a, b)$ implies $r(xay, xby)$ for all $x, y$. -/
def IsBiInvariant (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃a b : G⦄ (x y : G), r a b → r (x * a * y) (x * b * y)

/-- A group is *orderable* if it admits a bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G r ∧ IsBiInvariant r

/-- A group is *pro-orderable* (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 1.35) if every bi-invariant partial
order on it can be extended to a bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ r : G → G → Prop, IsPartialOrder G r → IsBiInvariant r →
    ∃ s : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G s ∧ IsBiInvariant s ∧ ∀ a b, r a b → s a b

/-- The order of a linearly ordered group is bi-invariant. -/
@[category test, AMS 6 20]
theorem isBiInvariant_le [LinearOrder G] [MulLeftMono G] [MulRightMono G] :
    IsBiInvariant (G := G) (· ≤ ·) :=
  fun _ _ x y h => mul_le_mul_left (mul_le_mul_right h x) y

/-- The group of integers is orderable. -/
@[category test, AMS 6 20]
theorem isOrderable_multiplicative_int : IsOrderable (Multiplicative ℤ) :=
  ⟨(· ≤ ·), inferInstance, isBiInvariant_le⟩

/-- Every pro-orderable group is orderable: extend the trivial partial order. -/
@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem IsProOrderable.isOrderable (h : IsProOrderable G) : IsOrderable G :=
  have : IsPartialOrder G Eq :=
    { refl := Eq.refl, trans := fun _ _ _ => Eq.trans, antisymm := fun _ _ h _ => h }
  let ⟨s, hs, hinv, _⟩ := h Eq this fun _ _ _ _ hab => by rw [hab]
  ⟨s, hs, hinv⟩

/--
Can every orderable group be embedded in a pro-orderable group?

That is, for every group $G$ admitting a bi-invariant linear order, is there a pro-orderable
group $H$ and an injective group homomorphism $G \to H$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.28» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsOrderable G →
      ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), IsProOrderable H ∧
        ∃ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.28»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 2.28

by A. I. Kokorin

Can every orderable group be embedded in a pro-orderable group?

Here an *orderable* group is a group admitting a linear order that is invariant
under multiplication on the left and on the right. Following Problem 1.35 of the
notebook (also by A. I. Kokorin), a group is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group in
the terminology of Fuchs) if every partial order on it that is invariant under
multiplication on the left and on the right can be extended to a linear order
with the same invariance. Since the trivial order is such a partial order, every
pro-orderable group is orderable.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.28»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A binary relation $r$ on a group $G$ is *bi-invariant* if $r(a, b)$ implies
$r(ca, cb)$ and $r(ac, bc)$ for all $a, b, c \in G$, i.e. it is preserved by
multiplication on the left and on the right. -/
def IsBiInvariant (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c : G, r a b → r (c * a) (c * b) ∧ r (a * c) (b * c)

/-- A group $G$ is *orderable* if it admits a bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ l : LinearOrder G, IsBiInvariant l.le

/-- A group $G$ is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group) if every bi-invariant partial order
$\preceq$ on $G$ can be extended to a bi-invariant linear order $\le$ on $G$, that is,
$a \preceq b$ implies $a \le b$ for all $a, b \in G$. -/
def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ p : PartialOrder G, IsBiInvariant p.le →
    ∃ l : LinearOrder G, IsBiInvariant l.le ∧ ∀ a b : G, p.le a b → l.le a b

/-- For the order relation of a type, bi-invariance is the conjunction of Mathlib's
`MulLeftMono` and `MulRightMono`. -/
@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem isBiInvariant_le_iff [LE G] :
    IsBiInvariant (fun a b : G => a ≤ b) ↔ MulLeftMono G ∧ MulRightMono G := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨⟨fun c a b hab => (h a b c hab).1⟩, ⟨fun c a b hab => (h a b c hab).2⟩⟩
  · rintro ⟨_, _⟩ a b c hab
    exact ⟨mul_le_mul_right hab c, mul_le_mul_left hab c⟩

/-- Every pro-orderable group is orderable: extend the trivial partial order. -/
@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem IsProOrderable.isOrderable (h : IsProOrderable G) : IsOrderable G := by
  let p : PartialOrder G :=
    { le := (· = ·)
      le_refl := fun _ => rfl
      le_trans := fun _ _ _ => Eq.trans
      le_antisymm := fun _ _ h _ => h }
  obtain ⟨l, hl, -⟩ := h p (by rintro a b c rfl; exact ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)
  exact ⟨l, hl⟩

/-- The infinite cyclic group is orderable. -/
@[category test, AMS 6 20]
theorem isOrderable_multiplicative_int : IsOrderable (Multiplicative ℤ) :=
  ⟨inferInstance, fun _ _ c hab => ⟨mul_le_mul_right hab c, mul_le_mul_left hab c⟩⟩

/--
Can every orderable group be embedded in a pro-orderable group?

An embedding is an injective group homomorphism; no compatibility with orders is required.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.28» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsOrderable G →
      ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), IsProOrderable H ∧ ∃ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.28»

Can every orderable group be embedded in a pro-orderable group?

Here an *orderable group* is a group admitting a linear order that is invariant under
multiplication on the left and on the right (a bi-invariant linear order). Following
Problem 1.35 of the Kourovka Notebook (also by A. I. Kokorin), a group is *pro-orderable* if
each of its (bi-invariant) partial orders can be extended to a (bi-invariant) linear order;
these are the $O^*$-groups of L. Fuchs. As in the theory of ordered groups, "partial order"
and "linear order" on a group always mean bi-invariant ones.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«2.28»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A binary relation $r$ on a group $G$ is *bi-invariant* if it is preserved by multiplication
on the left and on the right: $x \mathrel{r} y$ implies $ax \mathrel{r} ay$ and
$xa \mathrel{r} ya$ for all $a \in G$. For the relation `(· ≤ ·)` of an order on `G` this is
the conjunction of `MulLeftMono G` and `MulRightMono G`. -/
def IsBiInvariant (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ a x y, r x y → r (a * x) (a * y)) ∧ (∀ a x y, r x y → r (x * a) (y * a))

/-- A group is *orderable* if it admits a bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G r ∧ IsBiInvariant r

/-- A group is *pro-orderable* (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 1.35) if every bi-invariant
partial order on it can be extended to a bi-invariant linear order. Such groups are also
called $O^*$-groups. -/
def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ r : G → G → Prop, IsPartialOrder G r → IsBiInvariant r →
    ∃ s : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G s ∧ IsBiInvariant s ∧ ∀ x y, r x y → s x y

/-- Every pro-orderable group is orderable: extend the trivial partial order. -/
@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem IsProOrderable.isOrderable (h : IsProOrderable G) : IsOrderable G := by
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hinv, -⟩ := h (· = ·)
    { refl := fun _ => rfl
      trans := fun _ _ _ h₁ h₂ => h₁.trans h₂
      antisymm := fun _ _ h₁ _ => h₁ }
    ⟨fun a x y h => by rw [h], fun a x y h => by rw [h]⟩
  exact ⟨s, hs, hinv⟩

/--
Can every orderable group be embedded in a pro-orderable group?

That is, given a group $G$ admitting a bi-invariant linear order, is there a pro-orderable
group $H$ (every bi-invariant partial order on $H$ extends to a bi-invariant linear order,
see Problem 1.35) together with an injective group homomorphism $G \to H$? No compatibility
between orders is required of the embedding.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.28» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsOrderable G →
      ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), IsProOrderable H ∧
        ∃ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.28»

/-!
# Conjecture 2.28

by A. I. Kokorin

Can every orderable group be embedded in a pro-orderable group?

Here an *orderable* group is a group admitting a linear order that is invariant
under multiplication on both sides (an $O$-group). Following Problem 1.35 of the
notebook, a group is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group in the terminology of Fuchs)
if every partial order on it that is invariant under multiplication on both sides
can be extended to a linear order that is invariant under multiplication on both
sides. "Embedded" means embedded as an abstract group, i.e. there is an injective
group homomorphism; no compatibility with orders is required.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.28»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A binary relation $r$ on a group $G$ is *bi-invariant* if it is preserved by
multiplication on the left and on the right: $a \mathrel{r} b$ implies
$xa \mathrel{r} xb$ and $ax \mathrel{r} bx$ for all $x \in G$. -/
def IsBiInvariant (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃a b : G⦄, r a b → ∀ x : G, r (x * a) (x * b) ∧ r (a * x) (b * x)

/-- A group is *orderable* (an $O$-group) if it admits a bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsOrderableGroup : Prop :=
  ∃ r : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G r ∧ IsBiInvariant G r

/-- A group is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group in the terminology of Fuchs; see
Problem 1.35 of the Kourovka Notebook) if every bi-invariant partial order on it
can be extended to a bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsProOrderableGroup : Prop :=
  ∀ r : G → G → Prop, IsPartialOrder G r → IsBiInvariant G r →
    ∃ s : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G s ∧ IsBiInvariant G s ∧
      ∀ a b : G, r a b → s a b

/-- Every pro-orderable group is orderable: the trivial partial order (equality) extends
to a bi-invariant linear order. -/
@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem IsProOrderableGroup.isOrderableGroup (h : IsProOrderableGroup G) :
    IsOrderableGroup G := by
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hinv, -⟩ := h (· = ·) { antisymm := fun _ _ h _ => h }
    fun a b hab x => by subst hab; exact ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
  exact ⟨s, hs, hinv⟩

/--
Can every orderable group be embedded in a pro-orderable group?

That is, does every group $G$ admitting a bi-invariant linear order embed, via an
injective group homomorphism, into a group $H$ in which every bi-invariant partial
order extends to a bi-invariant linear order?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.28» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsOrderableGroup G →
      ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H), IsProOrderableGroup H ∧
        ∃ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.28»
